items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] Murdered for their eyes: people with albinism living in terror in Madagascar
items.content_html:
The country is struggling to address a rise in attacks, with a record 13 people – mostly children – killed this year for body parts, which some believe can bring good fortune

Not long after midnight in late May this year, three men barged through the door of the small room where Nicole Soalala lived with her family on the outskirts of Toliara, a coastal city in the south of Madagascar. Her husband got up to ask what they wanted, but they attacked him with a piece of wood and an axe.

Soalala, 32, grabbed her youngest child, Landricia – an 18-month-old girl with albinism – and hoisted her on to her back, holding her there with a piece of fabric she started to wrap around herself. Her eldest daughter, 15, hid under the table with her other two children, aged six and three.

Thirteen new feeds were onboarded this week, including technical and professional development sources (Two Minute Papers, The Pragmatic Engineer, HBR.org, Farnam Street), machine learning research (MIT News, DeepMind), design resources (UX Planet), and regional content from British Columbia and local news archives.
